overview: The CC Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) adjudicates petitions for variances, special permits, and findings under the Medford zoning ordinance. Since early 2023, the board has managed several large-scale Chapter 40B comprehensive permit developments, requiring extensive peer reviews of traffic, civil engineering, and architectural massing. Its routine business includes resolving residential disputes over fences, setbacks, and multi-family conversions. At its most recent sessions, the board has focused on interpreting new state regulations regarding accessory dwelling units and the conversion of non-conforming commercial spaces into residential or service-based uses.

threads.name: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway (Case 40B-2022-01)
threads.summary: The board conducted a multi-month review of this 350-unit development, beginning with peer reviews on traffic and architectural design. Discussions focused on fire safety, construction logistics, and the inclusion of public art in consultation with the Medford Arts Council. The board approved the comprehensive permit with conditions and a partial linkage fee waiver in July 2023. Recent design refinements, including the relocation of bike and trash rooms, were deemed insubstantial changes to the original permit.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway Residential Development (Case 40B-2023-01)
threads.summary: This 289-unit project underwent design changes to reduce building massing near residential neighbors and increase pervious open space. The board authorized detailed peer reviews for traffic and civil engineering before approving the comprehensive permit in May 2024. A partial linkage fee waiver was granted in exchange for off-site public improvements. Subsequently, the board approved a special permit for a lot split to maintain the coverage ratios for a separate on-site commercial building.

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs)
threads.summary: In early 2026, the board began evaluating petitions for accessory dwelling units under updated state zoning regulations. Petitions on Vassar Street and Wellesley Street have been continued to allow for legal counsel review and design modifications. The board is currently seeking to ensure these developments align with new guidelines while managing neighbor concerns regarding attic expansions and shed dormers.

citations.title: Attic Expansion and ADU Variance at 1-3 Vassar Street
citations.label: M54#3

threads.name: Cannabis Dispensary Permitting
threads.summary: The board originally approved a special permit for a retail dispensary at 114 Mystic Avenue in 2023. In 2026, the location received additional special permits for medical cannabis sales and product manufacturing under Victory Gardens. Following consultations with the police chief and legal counsel, the board also approved a special permit to allow courier delivery services from the facility.

threads.name: Residential Multi-Family Conversions
threads.summary: The board frequently hears petitions to convert single-family homes into two-family or three-family dwellings. While some requests are approved based on historical use records or topography hardships, others have been denied for failing to demonstrate a statutory hardship. Major projects in this category include the conversion of an auto repair shop into a three-unit townhouse on Elm Street and a historic restoration of a multi-family home on George Street.

threads.name: Administrative Appeals and Enforcement
threads.summary: The board adjudicates appeals of the building commissioner's decisions, such as the dismissal of an untimely residential alteration appeal. In 2026, the board heard a high-profile appeal regarding a notice of violation for a gutter business operating in a residential zone. After hearing testimony regarding noise and idling trucks, the board upheld the building commissioner's violation notice.

citations.title: 91 Waterville Road: Administrative Appeal of Notice of Violation
citations.label: M52#1

threads.name: Board Administration and Procedure
threads.summary: The board underwent several leadership changes, electing Mike Caldera as chair in 2023 and 2025, while Jamie Thompson served a term before resigning. Administrative efforts include updating the board's rules and regulations and moving meeting start times to 6:30 PM. To manage a backlog of minutes, the board has implemented new transcription and AI software tools.

citations.title: Administrative Updates and Rules of Order
citations.label: M09#7

periods.narrative: This period focused on the initial review and approval of the 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B project and several residential multi-family conversions.
The board processed the 970 Fellsway 40B application and addressed numerous residential variances for additions, fences, and parking flooding mitigation.
Recent work involves the interpretation of new state ADU laws and the expansion of cannabis dispensary operations to include delivery.
